name: Brussels
operatingHours: Brussels Metro (STIB) runs ~5:30 AM-~12:30 AM daily (last trains leave central stations around midnight). Trains every 3-5 min by day, 6-10 min evenings. No all-night metro; night buses (Noctis) run Fri-Sat. NMBS trains to the airport run ~5:00 AM-~midnight.
fareInfo: STIB single journey €2.40 by contactless card (2026), valid 1 hour with transfers; 24-hour and multi-day passes sold at stations and ticket machines. Airport trains are NMBS, not STIB: ~€12-15 one way to the city stations (includes the Diabolo airport supplement). Eurostar and Thalys/high-speed tickets are separate.

sights.name: Grand Place
sights.note: Brussels' guild-house square, ringed by gilded facades and the Gothic town hall; most atmospheric when lit at night.

sights.name: Royal Galleries of Saint-Hubert
sights.note: One of Europe's first glass-roofed arcades (1847), lined with chocolatiers, cafes and a cinema.
sights.hours: Arcade open 24 hours; shops ~10:00 AM-7:00 PM

sights.name: Atomium
sights.note: The 1958 World's Fair icon: nine linked steel spheres with exhibitions and a panoramic sphere at the top.

sights.name: Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula
sights.note: Brussels' Gothic cathedral with twin towers, stained glass and a free nave; the treasury and crypt charge a small fee.
sights.hours: ~7:00 AM-6:00 PM weekdays, shorter hours weekends

sights.name: Mini-Europe
sights.note: A park of 1:25 scale models of EU landmarks beside the Atomium; best with children.
sights.hours: Seasonal: ~10:00 AM-5:00/6:00 PM, closed some winter weeks

sights.name: Autoworld
sights.note: A large vintage-car museum under the Cinquantenaire's glass hall, from early motoring to classics.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM-5:00/6:00 PM daily (hours shift by season)

sights.name: Cinquantenaire Park
sights.note: Big landscaped park around a triumphal arch, with museums, lawns and a view to the Basilica from the arch.
sights.hours: Park open daily, sunrise to sunset

sights.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
sights.note: Old Masters and Flemish painting (Bruegel, Rubens) plus the Magritte Museum in one complex.
sights.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00 AM-5:00 PM, Sat-Sun 11:00 AM-6:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Brussels Town Hall
sights.note: Gothic civic palace on the Grand Place with a 96 m spire, visited on guided tours.
sights.hours: Guided visits on set days; check the tourism site

sights.name: Musical Instruments Museum (MIM)
sights.note: Thousands of instruments in a landmark Art Nouveau department store, with headphones that play the sounds.
sights.hours: Tue-Fri 9:30 AM-5:00 PM, Sat-Sun 10:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Church of Our Lady of the Sablon
sights.note: Flamboyant Gothic church in the antiques quarter, noted for its stained glass.

sights.name: Museum of Natural Sciences
sights.note: Europe's biggest dinosaur gallery, with Iguanodon skeletons found in Belgium.
sights.hours: Tue-Fri 9:30 AM-5:00 PM, Sat-Sun 10:00 AM-6:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Mont des Arts
sights.note: Terraced gardens between Central Station and the museum district with a good free city view.

sights.name: Cantillon Brewery
sights.note: A working lambic brewery and museum where you taste spontaneously fermented gueuze.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed Sun and some other days; check site

sights.name: Royal Palace of Brussels
sights.note: The monarchy's official palace facing Brussels Park; open to visitors only in summer, free.
sights.hours: Open to visitors ~late July to early Sept, Tue-Sun 10:30 AM-4:30 PM; closed rest of year

sights.name: Manneken Pis
sights.note: The tiny bronze fountain boy, famous for his many costumes; a quick photo stop.

sights.name: Place du Jeu de Balle flea market
sights.note: Daily flea market in the Marolles, local-flavor browsing among antiques and bric-a-brac.

sights.name: Place Poelaert viewpoint
sights.note: Free terrace in front of the Law Courts with a broad view across the lower town to the Atomium.

railStations.name: Brussels-Midi
railStations.note: The international hub: Eurostar to London (~2h) and Paris (~1h20), Thalys/high-speed to Amsterdam, Cologne and Paris, plus ICE and TGV and Belgian national trains. Metro lines 2 and 6 (Gare du Midi) and many trams stop here.

railStations.name: Brussels-Nord
railStations.note: Domestic and regional hub for Antwerp, Leuven and Ghent and many airport trains. Not on the metro map itself: Rogier station (Metro 2/6) is ~450 m south.

airports.name: Brussels Airport
airports.transitNote: NMBS trains from the airport reach Brussels-Nord in ~15 min, Brussels-Central in ~20 min and Brussels-Midi in ~25 min. Not on the metro map; buses 12 and 21 run to the EU Quarter (Schuman/Luxembourg). Taxi ~€45-55, 25-40 min.
